correctness.rationale: Every vertex at row i, column j has a distance-two neighbor in S iff at least two distinct columns contain a selected cell outside row i. This equivalence holds for selected vertices too. Partitioning the selected array by its number of multi-selected columns gives exact, disjoint contributions A, B and C, algebraically the claimed symmetric polynomial. The 3-vertex minimizers use 3 distinct rows and columns; when min(m,n)=2, each of its two fibers must contribute at least 2 cells. Exhaustive direct-neighborhood counting of 714,576 subsets agrees coefficientwise in 13 small dimensions, with a further 841 parameter tests. The finite tests are corroboration, not the proof.

value.rationale: Two-step domination models exact two-hop coverage and is computationally nontrivial on regular graphs; rook graphs form a canonical dense regular family. The theorem determines every labelled coefficient through one finite closed expression, much more than the previously established minimum total-domination number. The structural characterization also counts all optimal configurations, distinguishing the two-row boundary from the genuine three-way injective family. Such a cardinality distribution is a natural graph polynomial, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
